clue.text: Two card games one may come across

parts.note: the first game is the British name for blackjack or twenty-one
the second game is the partnership trick-taking game

explanation.surface: A puzzle about finding two card games that someone might happen to come across.
explanation.walkthrough: Both games come from the same three words: PONTOON (the British name for blackjack) followed by BRIDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating structure laid on boats lets troops or traffic cross a river, so people come across on it.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a name or form of address, as handle is slang for a name
second meaning: a legal entitlement, as to property

explanation.walkthrough: Handle looks like a verb, but here it is the slang noun for someone's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is a name or form of address, and also a legal claim of ownership to land or goods.

clue.text: One of us turns out to be unemployable

indicators.note: something that turns out a certain way has been made into a different shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A confession that one member of the group proves impossible to give a job to.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot be employed or put to work is useless, so it serves no purpose.

parts.note: taken as written; the Bard is Shakespeare

explanation.surface: Asks how to gauge Shakespeare's greatness.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no anagram word: the question mark warns that the letters of 'the Bard' must be rearranged, while the surface hints at the breadth of Shakespeare's genius.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadth is a dimension, the width of something, so it is a measurement taken across.

clue.text: Having no remedy but to suffer an island uprising

parts.note: to incur is to suffer or bring upon oneself

indicators.note: in a down clue a word rising goes up the column, so it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: A grim picture of islanders in revolt, with no option but to endure it.
explanation.definitionFit: An illness or problem that cannot be cured has no remedy at all.

clue.text: Gin that is a form of bottled spirits

indicators.note: a form of something is a reshaped version of it, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Gin described as a kind of spirit sold in bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: Spirits looks like alcohol, matching the gin; it means magical beings, like the genie trapped in Aladdin's lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Genii are the jinn of Arabian tales, magical beings often kept sealed in lamps or flasks.

definitions.meaning: first meaning, taken literally: wearing a perfect suit
second meaning: completely compatible as a couple

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is normally used of a well-matched couple; the first reading takes it literally, as clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple who match each other perfectly are said to be ideally suited, and a flawlessly tailored person is literally so.

parts.note: surface reading: sports winners playing an away match
setter's reading: medieval fighters who roamed far from home seeking adventure

explanation.walkthrough: Champions suggests title-holders in sport; here it means armoured warriors who fought on behalf of others, and errant means wandering.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval chivalric warriors who travelled the land championing causes were wanderers by definition.

clue.text: Be taunted about being a young socialite

indicators.note: letters moved about are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl mocked for being a society newcomer.
explanation.definitionFit: A deb is a young upper-class woman making her first formal appearance in fashionable society.

clue.text: Large kind of type in the chapter

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old printers' name for a large size of typeface
second meaning: a clergyman who is a member of a cathedral chapter

explanation.walkthrough: Chapter suggests a section of a book, fitting the printing theme; it is the body of clergy running a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Printers once named a big type size this way, and a cathedral's clergy body is made up of these priests.

indicators.note: the second piece is placed in the first, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: Abe is the familiar name of President Abraham Lincoln
the contraction I'd

explanation.surface: Someone saying they would be happy to remain in the English city of Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the cathedral city, but it is the American president.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide is to remain or dwell somewhere, an old-fashioned verb for staying put.

clue.text: Subordinate in a position lower than Heather

parts.note: beneath
ling is the common heather plant

explanation.surface: An office junior ranked below a colleague named Heather.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name; ling is the moorland shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of lower rank who takes orders is a junior or minion in the hierarchy.

parts.note: surface reading: a break-in or hacking incident
setter's reading: secret information escaping to the press, or fluid escaping through a hole

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a straight definition of a break-in; the answer is the seeping out of secrets or liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: When confidential material escapes to outsiders, or water seeps through a gap, containment has been breached.

clue.text: Right at the back, yet wanting the lion's share

parts.note: to be after something is to want it
the lion's share is the greatest part

explanation.surface: A paradox: someone hanging back at the rear while greedily wanting the biggest portion.
explanation.definitionFit: The furthest position astern on a ship, the hindmost part, is the rearmost one.

indicators.note: a name that changes is altered in form, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman named Tabitha moves house and changes her surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: The natural home or surroundings in which a creature lives is its habitat.

parts.note: surface reading: a contest that only a handful of entrants won
setter's reading: 'the Few' was Churchill's name for the RAF pilots who won the 1940 air war

explanation.walkthrough: Churchill said 'Never was so much owed by so many to so few' of the RAF fighter pilots of 1940, who became known as the Few.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1940 air campaign over southern England was won by the small band of RAF pilots called the Few.

indicators.note: letters set adrift float loose from their order and settle differently

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man cutting himself off from the world in a private retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a private den is where a man cuts himself adrift from others.
explanation.definitionFit: A private room or inner retreat where someone withdraws undisturbed, like a study or den.

parts.note: surface reading: a charge for leaving a car at a bank
setter's reading: the charge for tying a boat up at a river bank

explanation.walkthrough: Bank suggests a financial building with a car park; it is the side of a river where boats are tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid for the right to tie up a vessel at a berth or buoy is a mooring charge.

clue.text: Lead about a hundred into deep trouble

indicators.note: the first pieces are put into the last, so they sit inside it
something in trouble is disturbed, so its letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written
re means about or concerning
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone leading about a hundred people into serious difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: About a hundred reads like an approximate number; it is two separate pieces. Lead is the verb, rhyming with bead.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead is to go in front, coming before others in order or time.

indicators.note: meat that is minced is chopped into bits and mixed, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written; topside is a cut of beef

explanation.surface: A butcher's guess that a mince was made from topside, a lean cut of beef.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit something is to put it forward as a premise, taking it as given.

parts.note: to incur a cost is to get into it
IOUs are written promises of money owed

explanation.surface: Asks whether you would borrow money, and gets a firm refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: The question looks like an offer of a loan answered with a refusal; really the first three words split into two pieces and the reply is the definition. IOUs are notes acknowledging money owed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking curiosity shows no wish to find out about things.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to produce a network of fine cracks on a glaze or surface

explanation.walkthrough: Make cracks on suggests joking about a trend; it is the potter's term for crackling a glaze.
explanation.definitionFit: Pottery glazes develop fine cracks, a verb sense, and a brief enthusiasm sweeping the public is a fad.

clue.text: Yet this may increase a don's standing

definitions.text: Yet this may increase a don's standing

parts.words: Yet this may increase a don's standing
parts.note: surface reading: a paradox, since a seat stops you standing

parts.words: Yet this may increase a don's standing
parts.note: setter's reading: a professorship raises an academic's status

explanation.walkthrough: Yet points to the joke: something for sitting on that raises standing. A don is a university teacher, and a professorship is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: A professorship at a university is a seat of honour that raises an academic's status, as well as furniture for sitting.

clue.text: French writer quietly exits the academic field

indicators.note: the soft sign leaves, so that letter is taken out of the following word

parts.note: a university's grounds
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: A French author slipping quietly out of academia.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert Camus wrote The Outsider; removing the P from CAMPUS leaves him.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Camus was a Nobel-winning novelist and philosopher from French Algeria.

clue.text: She inspired the lyrics in the opera "Tosca"

indicators.note: the answer sits in the following words, running across their boundary

parts.note: the end of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.surface: Wondering who inspired Puccini's librettists in writing Tosca.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the nine Greek Muses, Erato presided over lyric and love poetry.

parts.note: surface reading: a versatile actor or all-rounder
setter's reading: a mechanical figure assembled from many components

explanation.walkthrough: A man of many parts is an idiom for a versatile person; here the parts are mechanical components.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot or mechanical figure built to imitate a human is made of many moving components.

clue.text: One gets down to the cleaning with this

definitions.text: One gets down to the cleaning with this

parts.words: One gets down to the cleaning with this
parts.note: surface reading: the tool you use to start a cleaning job

parts.words: One gets down to the cleaning with this
parts.note: setter's reading: down is soft plumage, so this cleaner is made of feathers

explanation.walkthrough: Gets down to sounds like starting work, but down is soft plumage on a cleaning implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A stick with a tuft of plumes on the end is used to flick dust off ornaments and shelves.
